title: KXO and Gyeongju pursue 2027 FIBA 3x3 tournament bid
text:
KXO and Gyeongju pursue 2027 FIBA 3x3 tournament bid - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 19일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports KXO and Gyeongju pursue 2027 FIBA 3x3 tournament bid 
 입력 2026.11.19. 17:50 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 KXO and the city of Gyeongju have begun taking concrete steps to host a 2027 FIBA 3x3 international tournament. Drawing on their successful experience hosting 3x3 events in Gyeongju over the past two years, they are now pursuing an international tournament.
 A meeting of officials to discuss a bid to host a FIBA 3x3 international tournament was held in the mayor's office at Gyeongju City Hall on the 18th. Attendees, including Gyeongju Mayor Joo Nak-young, Deputy Mayor Choi Hyuk-jun, Culture and Tourism Bureau Director Nam Mi-kyung and Choi Hee-am, chairman of the KXO International Tournament Organizing Committee, discussed ways to secure the event and plans for moving forward.
 Gyeongju has hosted the KXO 3x3 Gyeongju STOP at a temporary court in Daereungwon since 2025. After successfully holding the event for two consecutive years, the city has seen the commercial potential of 3x3 basketball and the competitive strength of sports events that combine the sport with local tourism resources.
 The participation of overseas teams raised the level of play and drew greater international interest. Responses from Korean players and their families were also positive. Student athletes and their parents who visited Gyeongju took in local historical and cultural attractions, including Daereungwon, alongside competing in the tournament, enjoying both sports and tourism.
 Building on these results, Gyeongju plans to pursue hosting a larger 3x3 international tournament in 2027.
 Gyeongju Mayor Joo Nak-young gave a positive assessment of the city's experience hosting the event over the past two years. "I visited the venue and watched the games in person, and I was struck by 3x3's popularity and dynamic play," Joo said. "We want to build on our experience hosting the tournament over the past two years and try to bring a somewhat larger 3x3 international event to Gyeongju next year."
 "Chairperson Choi Hee-am and President Park Geon-yeon have been giving us a lot of help. KXO staff, who are experts in 3x3, began working early to bring an international tournament here, and Gyeongju will also cooperate actively to achieve a good result," he added.
 KXO is also moving quickly to prepare for the bid. Choi Hee-am, chairperson of the KXO International Tournament Organizing Committee, said discussions with FIBA on related proposals have already begun.
 "Gyeongju has historical significance internationally, so I believe hosting a 3x3 international tournament could create even greater tangible and intangible value," Choi said. "We will prepare diligently so we can hold a great 3x3 international tournament in Gyeongju next year."
 Attention is focused on whether KXO and Gyeongju can secure the international tournament, drawing on two years of experience running events together. The question is whether the historic cultural city of Gyeongju can make its mark on the international sports stage through 3x3 basketball.
